norms.what: A stage skill is model-invocable so the orchestrator can start it, which also lets Claude invoke it on an unrelated task; the run-file guard makes that cost one skill load. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #38). In 0.6.0 the run's files moved from `.claude/audits/` to their own folder under `.model-audits/`: Claude Code protects all of `.claude/` from writes in every permission mode but bypass, and allow rules do not pre-approve them, so a headless smoke run in `acceptEdits` stopped before the plan and every user outside auto mode got a prompt per write (#57).
After compaction the orchestrator, the oldest skill of the run, is the first to be dropped; re-invoking it restores the run's standing rules. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #38).

The traps are the largest part of a knowledge file and only the traps stage needs them, so the plan reads the file only down to them. A bootstrap has no knowledge file, so its docs come from the documentation index and the user confirms them. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #38). The plan no longer reads a docs table or runs a bootstrap from the documentation index; it takes the date the knowledge was verified, which the plan now shows. Since #105 the audit reaches no network: the directory's validation flagged the run-time fetch, and what a published plugin reads has to be in the reviewed commit.

Added after the gate's estimate proved far too low. The old estimate was the inventory times one to three, plus 30–40k for the skills, but the inventory is a small part of a run: the fixed load (harness, the audit's own skills, the knowledge file) is ~75–85k, the docs ~30k, each finding costs its writing, relabelling, verification and report entry, and every verifier loads its own base and opens the cached pages to check passages. Each row's coefficients come from two runs of this audit at full scope in session mode: a small seeded project (inventory ~18k tokens, 10 batches, 74 raw findings, 3 verifiers) whose gate said ~65k–125k and which spent ~243k tokens of context in the session and ~248k in the verifiers, US$7.90, 18 min; and a tiny throwaway project (~0.2k, 1 batch, 8 findings, 1 verifier) whose gate said ~30–40k and which spent ~116k and ~40k, US$2.16, 4.5 min. Recomputed from what each plan knew, the rows bracket both: ~221k–565k against ~490k, and ~148k–201k against ~156k. The range is wide because the number of findings is unknown until the files are read (#34, #59). The docs row, sized from the pages the retired `N17` measured, became the digest row, sized from the shipped change digest (`G`), and the verifier's rows count the digest where they counted cached pages. These formulas were calibrated on runs that fetched the pages and have not been re-measured since (#108).

Added with the close's stray-file check (#61). The close can only tell which files the run created or changed when it knows the root's state before the run, including files the user had already left untracked; the record lives in the run's folder (#34).

In 0.6.2 (#87), a live session-mode run on the Sonnet fixture stopped mid-discovery with `stop_reason: "refusal"`, category `reasoning_extraction`, after reading the lines the reasoning-in-the-reply trap (Opus P04, Sonnet P09) exists to find; the guides say such requests can be declined, and Claude Code's automatic fallback covers other categories only, so the run simply stopped. Only the plan can find those lines before any file is read, and `grep | cut -d: -f1,2` returns line numbers without the lines, so nothing of their text reaches the context. The maintainer kept the session-mode recommendation (#87): with the lines never read, the cause is gone in both modes, so the plan only states how many lines are cited by number and that a refusal costs at most one batch. The pattern lives in the knowledge file's `<unquoted>` block, above `<traps>`, which is all the plan reads of it; on both fixtures it matches exactly the planted lines and nothing else.

In 0.6.2 (#89), the Opus live demo on the fixture had 5 of 11 `batch-auditor` agents refused on their first request, before any file was read: a rule with no `paths:` frontmatter that holds a line of the reasoning-in-the-reply trap (Opus P04) is loaded at launch, and every session and subagent of the project carries it, so no split of the batch could help. The memory page says rules without `paths` are loaded at launch like `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, and the sub-agents page lists the CLAUDE.md hierarchy and project rules among what a subagent loads at startup; one passage of the same page says memory still loads even where `omitClaudeMd` is set, so the plan states the risk ("likely") rather than a certainty. The plan cannot read the file to see its frontmatter (that could be the line itself), so it counts the `^paths:` lines with `grep -c`, which prints a number only. The recovery is in [transition-audit#N21]: the session reads those batches itself. The session-mode recommendation stays as the maintainer decided in #87.
